cues.en: Would you like something to drink?
cues.zh: 你想喝点什么吗？

cues.en: I'll go with a cup of coffee, please.
cues.zh: 我想要一杯咖啡，谢谢。

cues.en: Would you like a pour-over or an espresso?
cues.zh: 你想要手冲咖啡还是意式浓缩咖啡？

cues.en: A pour-over, please. What do you recommend?
cues.zh: 请给我一杯手冲咖啡。你有什么推荐？

cues.en: This one has notes of orange and dark chocolate.
cues.zh: 这款带有橙子和黑巧克力的风味。

cues.en: That sounds great. I'll take it without milk.
cues.zh: 听起来不错。我想喝不加奶的。

cues.en: Leftover rice can make excellent fried rice the next day.
cues.zh: 隔夜的米饭第二天可以做成很棒的炒饭。

cues.en: Cold rice is easier to separate, so it gives the dish a better texture.
cues.zh: 冷饭更容易拨散，所以炒出来的口感更好。

cues.en: Start with a hot pan and add a little oil.
cues.zh: 先把锅烧热，再加一点油。

cues.en: A handful of chopped vegetables adds color and helps use up what is in the fridge.
cues.zh: 一把切碎的蔬菜既能增添颜色，也能消耗冰箱里的食材。

cues.en: A splash of soy sauce can bring out the savory flavor.
cues.zh: 加一点酱油就能提鲜。

cues.en: If the rice was left at room temperature for too long, throw it away.
cues.zh: 如果米饭在室温下放得太久，就把它丢掉。

cues.en: Two people can taste the same soup and describe it in completely different ways.
cues.zh: 两个人喝同一碗汤，描述却可能截然不同。

cues.en: That is partly because flavor combines taste, aroma, and texture.
cues.zh: 部分原因在于风味融合了味觉、香气和口感。

cues.en: Temperature matters too: frozen desserts often seem sweeter as they warm up.
cues.zh: 温度也很重要：冷冻甜点回温后，常常让人觉得更甜。

cues.en: Professional tasters build a vocabulary by comparing small samples side by side.
cues.zh: 专业品尝者通过对照品尝少量样品来积累描述风味的词汇。

cues.en: You can train your palate at home by trying to pick out just one unfamiliar note.
cues.zh: 在家里，你可以试着从食物中辨别一种陌生的风味，来训练自己的味觉。

cues.en: The goal is to notice more, even when you disagree with someone else's description.
cues.zh: 目标是留意到更多细节，即使你不同意别人的描述。

cues.en: Good morning. I'd like to check in for my flight.
cues.zh: 早上好。我想办理登机手续。

cues.en: May I see your passport and booking confirmation?
cues.zh: 我可以看一下你的护照和预订确认单吗？

cues.en: Of course. Do you still have a window seat available?
cues.zh: 当然。还有靠窗的座位吗？

cues.en: Yes, there is one near the back of the plane.
cues.zh: 有一个，在飞机后部。

cues.en: That works for me. What time does boarding start?
cues.zh: 没问题。几点开始登机？

cues.en: Boarding starts at nine fifteen, at gate twelve.
cues.zh: 九点一刻开始登机，在十二号登机口。

title: One day in a walkable city
zh: 在适合步行的城市待一天

cues.en: The best way to get to know this neighborhood is on foot.
cues.zh: 了解这个街区最好的方式就是步行。

cues.en: Instead of following the main road, take a detour through the market.
cues.zh: 可以绕进市场走一走，避开主路。

cues.en: Most of the stalls open early and sell something local.
cues.zh: 大多数摊位开得很早，也会卖一些当地特色商品。

cues.en: Leave enough time to stop when something catches your eye.
cues.zh: 留出足够的时间，遇到感兴趣的东西就可以停下来看看。

cues.en: If you get tired, look for a bench by the river.
cues.zh: 如果走累了，可以找一张河边的长椅。

cues.en: With no rigid schedule, a wrong turn can become the best part of the day.
cues.zh: 行程宽松时，走错路也可能成为当天最精彩的部分。

title: Rethinking a packed itinerary
zh: 重新考虑排得太满的行程

cues.en: A packed itinerary can make a short trip feel surprisingly exhausting.
cues.zh: 排得太满的行程会让一趟短途旅行也异常疲惫。

cues.en: Every extra stop comes with a trade-off, even if it is only a few minutes away.
cues.zh: 每多去一处都需要有所取舍，哪怕那里只有几分钟路程。

cues.en: You may spend more time checking transport schedules than looking around.
cues.zh: 你花在查交通时刻表上的时间，可能比观光还多。

cues.en: One solution is to choose a single anchor activity for each day.
cues.zh: 一种办法是每天只安排一项主要活动。

cues.en: Then keep the rest of the day open for places you discover along the way.
cues.zh: 然后把剩下的时间留给途中偶然发现的地方。

cues.en: Planning for that flexibility is often what makes a trip feel spontaneous.
cues.zh: 提前留出这种弹性，反而常常能让旅行更有随性探索的感觉。

cues.en: A headline tells you what a news story is about.
cues.zh: 新闻标题告诉你一篇报道讲的是什么。

cues.en: It usually gives the main point in just a few words.
cues.zh: 它通常只用几个词就概括了要点。

cues.en: A short headline cannot tell you every detail.
cues.zh: 简短的标题无法告诉你所有细节。

cues.en: Read the first few paragraphs to find out what happened.
cues.zh: 读一读开头几段，了解发生了什么。

cues.en: Check when the story was published before you share it.
cues.zh: 分享前看一看报道是什么时候发布的。

cues.en: An old story can sound new when you see it without a date.
cues.zh: 没有日期时，旧新闻也可能看起来像刚发生的事。

title: A closer look at a survey

cues.en: A survey result can sound more certain than it really is.
cues.zh: 调查结果听起来可能比实际更确定。

cues.en: Before you trust the number, look at the sample size.
cues.zh: 相信这个数字前，先看看样本量。

cues.en: A survey of fifty people tells you less than a well-designed survey of five thousand.
cues.zh: 与一项设计严谨的五千人调查相比，五十人的调查能说明的问题更少。

cues.en: It also matters how the respondents were chosen.
cues.zh: 受访者是如何选出来的，这同样重要。

cues.en: A question posted in one online group may attract people who already agree.
cues.zh: 在一个网络群组内发起的提问，可能吸引的是本来就持类似观点的人。

cues.en: The next time you see a percentage, ask who was counted and who was left out.
cues.zh: 下次看到百分比时，问问有哪些人被统计在内，哪些人被遗漏了。

cues.en: In a developing story, two reputable outlets can report different details.
cues.zh: 在一则仍在发展的新闻中，两家信誉良好的媒体也可能报道不同的细节。

cues.en: One reporter may have a firsthand account, while another is quoting an official statement.
cues.zh: 一位记者可能掌握了第一手叙述，而另一位引用的是官方声明。

cues.en: Those accounts can both be useful, but neither necessarily contains the whole picture.
cues.zh: 这两种信息都可能有用，但任何一种都未必涵盖全貌。

cues.en: Look for independent sources that corroborate the most important claims.
cues.zh: 寻找能够独立印证关键说法的信息来源。

cues.en: When a fact is still uncertain, responsible outlets will say what they could verify.
cues.zh: 某个事实尚无定论时，负责任的媒体会说明自己核实了哪些信息。

cues.en: Waiting for an update can be the fastest way to avoid believing the wrong thing.
cues.zh: 等一等后续消息，可能反而是避免误信的最快方法。

cues.en: A battery stores energy that your phone can use later.
cues.zh: 电池储存能量，供手机之后使用。

cues.en: The screen uses some of that energy whenever it lights up.
cues.zh: 屏幕每次亮起都会消耗一些能量。

cues.en: Apps can also use power while you are doing something else.
cues.zh: 在你做别的事情时，应用也可能在耗电。

cues.en: If you turn down the brightness, your battery may last longer.
cues.zh: 如果你调低屏幕亮度，电池可能更耐用。

cues.en: When your phone runs down, plug it in and give it time to charge.
cues.zh: 手机没电时，插上电源，给它一点时间充电。

cues.en: How long it takes depends on the charger and the phone.
cues.zh: 要充多久取决于充电器和手机。

title: What a smart thermostat learns
zh: 智能恒温器能学到什么

cues.en: A smart thermostat can learn when a household usually comes and goes.
cues.zh: 智能恒温器可以了解一家人通常什么时候出门和回家。

cues.en: It uses that pattern to adjust the temperature automatically.
cues.zh: 它利用这一规律自动调节温度。

cues.en: During the day, it may turn the heating down while nobody is home.
cues.zh: 白天家里没人时，它可能会调低供暖温度。

cues.en: Before you return, it can start warming the room again.
cues.zh: 在你回来之前，它可以重新给房间升温。

cues.en: The savings depend on your home and how you used to heat it.
cues.zh: 能节省多少取决于你家的条件，以及你过去怎样供暖。

cues.en: The simplest way to check is to compare energy bills over a similar period.
cues.zh: 最简单的检验方法，就是比较相似时段的能源账单。

title: Why translation tools miss the joke
zh: 翻译工具为什么抓不住笑点

cues.en: An accurate translation can still miss the point of a joke.
cues.zh: 即使翻译准确，仍可能没抓住一个笑话的笑点。

cues.en: Wordplay often depends on a word having two meanings at once.
cues.zh: 文字游戏往往依赖一个词同时具有两种含义。

cues.en: In another language, the two meanings may require completely different words.
cues.zh: 换成另一种语言，两种含义可能需要用完全不同的词来表达。

cues.en: A literal translation can preserve the information while losing the surprise.
cues.zh: 直译可能保留了信息，却丢掉了反转带来的惊喜。

cues.en: A translator may create new wordplay to produce a comparable effect.
cues.zh: 译者可能会创造新的文字游戏，以取得类似效果。

cues.en: That is one reason to read subtitles alongside the original dialogue.
cues.zh: 这也是将字幕和原始对白对照着看的一条理由。

cues.en: Before email, people often wrote letters by hand.
cues.zh: 在电子邮件出现之前，人们经常手写信件。

cues.en: They put the letter in an envelope and took it to the post office.
cues.zh: 他们把信装进信封，再带到邮局。

cues.en: A letter could take days or even weeks to arrive.
cues.zh: 一封信可能需要数天甚至数周才能送到。

cues.en: Some families kept letters for many years.
cues.zh: 有些家庭把这些信保存了许多年。

cues.en: Even the handwriting can tell us something about the person who wrote the letter.
cues.zh: 连笔迹也能让我们了解写信人的一些情况。

cues.en: Reading a letter can make the past feel closer.
cues.zh: 读一封旧信能让我们感觉离过去更近。

cues.en: Different towns once set their clocks according to local solar time.
cues.zh: 过去，不同城镇曾按照当地的太阳时校准时钟。

cues.en: That worked when most people rarely traveled between distant places.
cues.zh: 在大多数人很少进行长途旅行的年代，这种方式行得通。

cues.en: Railways made different local times a problem for anyone writing a timetable.
cues.zh: 铁路出现后，各地时间不同就成了编制时刻表的人要面对的问题。

cues.en: A train could appear to leave one station before it arrived at the previous one.
cues.zh: 按各站的当地时间看，一辆火车甚至可能在抵达上一站前就从下一站发车。

cues.en: Standard times helped railways coordinate journeys across longer distances.
cues.zh: 标准时间帮助铁路协调更长距离的旅程。

cues.en: The clocks we use today still reflect that need to coordinate.
cues.zh: 我们今天使用的时钟仍体现了这种协调的需要。

cues.en: A map can tell us as much about its maker as it does about the land itself.
cues.zh: 一张地图既能让我们了解土地，也能让我们了解制图者。

cues.en: A merchant might care about roads, ports, and market towns.
cues.zh: 一位商人可能关心道路、港口和集镇。

cues.en: Someone working for a government may instead draw boundaries that show control.
cues.zh: 为政府工作的人可能更关心画出能体现管辖范围的边界。

cues.en: The things a map leaves out can be just as revealing as the details it includes.
cues.zh: 地图省略的东西，可能和它绘出的细节一样能说明问题。

cues.en: Historians ask who commissioned the map and what its intended users needed to know.
cues.zh: 历史学家会问是谁委托绘制地图，以及目标使用者需要知道什么。

cues.en: That helps explain why maps of the same place can look so different.
cues.zh: 这有助于解释为什么绘制的是同一个地方，地图却大相径庭。

cues.en: Do you have two tickets for the seven o'clock show?
cues.zh: 晚上七点那场还有两张票吗？

cues.en: Sorry, that show is sold out, but there is another at eight thirty.
cues.zh: 抱歉，那场卖完了，不过八点半还有一场。

cues.en: Are there any seats near the middle of the room?
cues.zh: 放映厅中间附近还有座位吗？

cues.en: I have two in the fifth row, next to the aisle.
cues.zh: 第五排还有两个，挨着过道。

cues.en: Perfect. I'll take both of them.
cues.zh: 太好了。我两张都要。

cues.en: Enjoy the movie, and keep your tickets until you are inside.
cues.zh: 祝你观影愉快，进场前请保管好电影票。

cues.en: A film can build suspense before anything unusual appears on screen.
cues.zh: 电影可以在画面中出现异常之前就营造出悬念。

cues.en: Imagine a character walking down an empty hallway.
cues.zh: 想象一位角色走过空荡荡的走廊。

cues.en: At first, the only sound is the steady rhythm of footsteps.
cues.zh: 起初，唯一的声音是节奏稳定的脚步声。

cues.en: Then the soundtrack adds a low note that almost feels like a warning.
cues.zh: 随后配乐加入一个低音，几乎像在发出警告。

cues.en: If that note suddenly stops, the silence can feel even more unsettling.
cues.zh: 如果低音突然消失，寂静可能让人更加不安。

cues.en: The choices the audience barely notices can have the strongest effect.
cues.zh: 观众几乎没察觉的声音安排，有时反而最有感染力。

title: Why an adaptation changes the story

cues.en: Readers sometimes feel disappointed when a film changes a scene from a favorite novel.
cues.zh: 当电影改动了心爱小说中的一幕，读者有时会觉得失望。

cues.en: But a novel and a film offer different ways to show what a character is thinking.
cues.zh: 不过，小说和电影展现人物想法的方式不同。

cues.en: A page of inner monologue can tell readers things that a camera cannot record directly.
cues.zh: 一页内心独白能告诉读者一些镜头无法直接拍摄的信息。

cues.en: An adaptation might show those thoughts through a gesture, a silence, or a different scene.
cues.zh: 改编作品可能通过一个动作、一阵沉默或另一个场景来表现这些想法。

cues.en: That can change the details of the story while keeping its emotional shape.
cues.zh: 这样既可能改变故事的细节，也可能保留其情感走向。

cues.en: A good comparison asks what each version makes possible.
cues.zh: 好的比较会问，每个版本各自实现了什么。
